## Phase 2 — Agent and skills (round 1)

Status: APPROVED

- [medium] agents/ship-pm.md:90: The handover verb says "Commit only files the repo already tracks, so a gitignored .project-manager/ stays gitignored." This conflates "not gitignored" with "already tracked". In a repo where .project-manager/ is tracked (which the dogfood in task 10 creates here), newly written state files — STATUS.md, CONVENTIONS.md, decisions/*.md, a regenerated dashboard.html — are untracked but not ignored, so this rule tells the agent to skip them on every handover. They would never be committed, and the intended protection (do not commit into a gitignored directory) is not what the sentence actually implements. — recorded
- [medium] skills/pm/SKILL.md:51: Dashboard freshness is asserted in the skill ("After any verb that changed state, the agent regenerates .project-manager/dashboard.html per the pm-state procedure") but agents/ship-pm.md never mentions dashboard.html — not in the HARD-GATE, not in the "Where the truth lives" table, and not in the status/groom/check/handover sections. Step 4 delegates by passing only the matching verb brief plus raw $ARGUMENTS, so the regeneration instruction never reaches the agent. After a groom or check that rewrites ROADMAP.md, the dashboard silently shows stale priorities/blockers, which contradicts the layer's "never invent status" premise. — recorded
- [medium] skills/pm/SKILL.md:26: Step 4 says free-text questions are delegated "passing the matching verb brief below verbatim plus the raw $ARGUMENTS", but only four briefs exist (status/groom/check/handover) — there is no brief for free-text questions or the bare brief. The load-bearing routing semantics (recommend exactly one item: highest-priority non-done, non-blocked item whose Depends-on items are all done; parallel lanes; decision/history from DECISIONS.md + decisions/) live at lines 38-47 under the heading "## Bare brief (no arguments)", so the free-text path is not directed to them, and agents/ship-pm.md's free-text section (line 97) is a single generic sentence that omits all of it. "What should I work on next?" — the flagship documented use case — may therefore be answered without the recorded rule that the previous read-only skill applied inline. — recorded
- [medium] skills/pm-sync/SKILL.md:55: Reconcile step 2 states unconditionally that STATUS.md's `## In flight`, `## Recently shipped`, and `## Repo hygiene` sections "are also refreshed from reality", but it runs before step 3's Growth path (line 57), which is the gate that asks the user once before creating STATUS.md in a legacy v5.3.0 directory. Against a legacy directory with no STATUS.md, step 2 as written pushes toward creating the file without confirmation, which contradicts skills/pm-state/SKILL.md:201 ("/ship:pm-sync reconcile is the only path that grows an old directory into the new shape, and it does so with the user's confirmation. Nothing auto-migrates."). — recorded
- [low] skills/help/SKILL.md:29: The help listing still describes the command as `/ship:pm "question"  Ask the project manager: next item, parallel work, status, decisions`, which no longer reflects the verb-driven interface (status / groom / check <feature> / handover / bare brief). Task 9 in phase 3 updates CLAUDE.md and CHANGELOG.md but does not list skills/help/SKILL.md, so this line will ship stale. — recorded
- [low] agents/ship-pm.md:1: ship-pm's handover verb makes atomic git commits, but its frontmatter omits `skills: - git-commits`, which both other committing agents declare (agents/ship-builder.md and agents/ship-verifier.md preload the git-commits reference skill). The agent instead relies on prose ("following the repo's commit convention"), so it will not have the shared commit-message rules loaded. This matches the plan's literal frontmatter block, so it is a plan-inherited gap rather than a builder deviation. — recorded
